title: Equivalence and nonequivalence between shared-phreatic storage coupling and lower-boundary-head coupling
purpose: Establish mathematically when a lower-boundary exchange formulation can reproduce the same phreatic head as a one-state h-link, while preserving the distinction between the two coupling contracts.

shared_phreatic.numerical_representation: MODFLOW STO owns the combined storage once; API contributes only the external input

zero_resistance_boundary.state: the imposed lower-boundary head is algebraically identical to the groundwater head for this manufactured limit
zero_resistance_boundary.numerical_representation: MODFLOW STO owns S_groundwater; API publishes the mass-complete column bottom exchange

gates: shared-phreatic and zero-resistance boundary formulations each converge in live MODFLOW and both reproduce 8.05 m within 1e-10 m
their total external-input and storage ledgers each close within 1e-12 m
the finite-resistance formulation reproduces the independent two-reservoir closed form within 1e-10 m
finite-resistance H_column and H_groundwater are distinct and neither equals the 8.05 m shared-state solution within 1e-3 m
a high-conductance control C=1000/day approaches the 8.05 m shared-head limit within 1e-5 m
interpretation_rules: Equal numerical heads in the zero-resistance manufactured limit establish conditional equation equivalence, not identity of coupling architecture.
The equivalence requires the boundary exchange to include the column storage response exactly once.
Finite interface resistance introduces a second physical head and breaks one-state h-link equivalence.
Current production F-GC is not reclassified as phreatic shared-state by this test; MAP11/MAP12 remain the domain/semantics authority.
forbidden: no inference that current F-GC has zero physical resistance
no inference that MODFLOW STO and real SWAP storage overlap in a deployment without explicit domain ownership
no reuse of MetaSWAP numerical coefficients as SWAP5 authority
